A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DPL and share the principal method and experiments despite the changed title and author list. All pages, equations, figures, and tables were readable. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 report original DPL benchmark results, timing measurements, missing-modality robustness experiments, and component ablations.

after.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report retained and additional original experiments, including evaluations without prompt tuning, ViLT comparisons, and new ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use missing-case-selected, modality-decomposed class prototypes, cosine scoring, case-specific ArcFace parameters, and a prototype contrastive penalty. LSupCon is renamed and reexpressed as LPRC. The additional backbone and no-prompt evaluations do not establish a substantive redesign of DPL.

E1.justification: Both evaluate movie genre classification on MM-IMDb, food classification on UPMC Food-101, and hate detection on Hateful Memes under image-missing, text-missing, and mixed-missing conditions. The added model configurations and controls reuse this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a standalone FC baseline without prompt tuning and adds MAP comparisons to the missing-rate robustness experiment. DePT is removed from the MaPLe and Hateful Memes comparisons; its main benchmark comparison is retained for MAP/DCP on Food-101 in Table 3, alongside robustness comparisons on MM-IMDb. Renaming the default heads as FC does not itself introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds head-only training without prompts, ViLT evaluation with 16-token prompts, minimum-entropy selection controls, and margin/lambda sweeps. It also reports AdamW instead of v1's Adam, although this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The principal benchmark metrics and 50/70/90% missing-rate design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds missing-awareness removal experiments using minimum-entropy selection (Table 5), hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figure 5), and MAP missing-rate robustness curves. The timing study is removed. The loss/decomposition questions remain, but v1's component-ablation results are replaced by Table 4, whose Hateful Memes/no-prompt labeling conflicts with the MM-IMDb/DCP discussion.

E5.justification: v1's timing means, standard-deviation error bars, and statement of ten independent timing runs disappear with its Figure 5. Both versions retain ten random missingness simulations and performance boxplots, without adding confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds standalone, ViLT, MAP robustness, missing-awareness, and hyperparameter results while replacing component-ablation results and removing timing and many DePT entries. Retained Table 1 scores match except that DCP+DPL on Hateful Memes at 70% mixed missingness changes from 67.57 to 67.68 AUROC. The new results concern additional configurations and should not be interpreted as same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 explicitly defines multiclass ArcFace and its multilabel extension in Equations 8 and 10–11; v2 removes these mathematical definitions and describes ArcFace verbally. The prototype and cosine-scoring mathematics remains substantially equivalent, and the contrastive expression uses more explicit class/case/modality indexing. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that a missing-aware prototype head improves robustness remains. v2 additionally makes standalone effectiveness without prompt tuning an explicit contribution in the introduction and conclusion, extending v1's emphasis on integration with prompt-based methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving prototype drift, balancing case-specific decision boundaries, insufficient regularization at small lambda, and robustness when missing-awareness is disabled. v1's dataset-specific modality-importance and low-overhead interpretations disappear. The new claim that missing-awareness consistently benefits DPL is stronger than Table 5 supports, which includes negative deltas of -0.03 and -0.23.

D1.justification: v2 documents the official MAP/ViLT implementation, its 16-token prompts, and the margin/lambda sweep settings. It drops v1's explicit first-six-layer prompt placement and EOT/CLS pooling description. These omissions reduce implementation detail without establishing that those procedures changed; the main CLIP dimensions, batch size, and GPU remain documented.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around missing-modality prompting, prediction-level adaptation, and prototype learning. It adds discussion of MSP and MuAP, incomplete multimodal prototype research, and recent/concurrent prototype methods for OOD detection and domain shift, alongside broader prompt-learning and application context. These literature additions are distinct from evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and substantial portions of the method and results narrative are rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 4 to Section 2, and the method is reorganized into workflow, problem definition, prototype formulation, scoring, and learning subsections. Terminology and the author block also change.

P2.justification: The introductory and framework illustrations are replaced by new Figures 1–2. Table 1 is restructured around FC/DPL pairs and standalone results, with selected DePT comparisons moved to Table 3. The component ablations are combined into a replacement table, robustness plots are redesigned or relocated, and new backbone, missing-awareness, and hyperparameter displays are added while the timing chart is removed.

improvement.justification: The standalone and ViLT evaluations provide useful evidence beyond v1's prompt-tuned CLIP experiments, and the revised exposition clarifies the prediction-head contribution. However, v2 removes timing evidence and explicit multilabel-loss definitions. Its replacement ablation table conflicts with the text about dataset, model, and metric, while Table 5 contradicts the claim of consistently positive missing-awareness effects. These reporting and reproducibility losses make the net benefit of the expanded evidence uncertain.
